question.leadin: This country joined the European Union in 1995, and opened the Oresund Bridge in 2000, which connected its city of Malmo to Denmark.
question.text: Name this country, whose Prime Minister Olof Palme was assassinated in 1986 while walking from a movie with his wife. Ingvar Carlsson succeeded Palme as Prime Minister of this country.
question.clue: A chemist from this country was nicknamed the "merchant of death" for inventing dynamite.

swap.text: As part of Operation Wrath of God, Israeli agents killed an innocent waiter in this country, believing him to be one of the perpetrators of the Munich massacre. The Kalmar Union included this country and its eastern neighbor Sweden.
swap.clue: After referenda in 1974 and 1992, this country, like Switzerland, declined to join the E.U.

question.leadin: A sniper from this country, Simo Hayha, gained the nickname "White Death" for killing hundreds of Soviet troops without using a scope during the Winter War.
question.text: Name this country whose fallen soldiers are often buried in the Hietaniemi Cemetery in Helsinki.
question.answerHtml: Finland [or Republic of Findland or Suomen tasavalta or Republiken Finland or Suomi]
question.clue: Its two invasions by Russia were known as the Greater Wrath and the Lesser Wrath.

swap.text: This Norwegian terrorist set off a car bomb in Oslo and carried out a mass shooting in Utoya, which he claimed to do in order to fight against the forces of Islam and multiculturalism.
swap.clue: First, name this right-wing extremist who was also responsible for the Utoya massacre, in which he opened fire on a crowd, killing 69 and injuring 66 at an AUF summer camp.

question.text: This man was Minister-President under Josef Terboven after the Nazis removed him from control of his own Fascist state. This Norwegian statesman's surname has become a synonym for "traitor."
question.clue: This man made a 7:32 PM broadcast in NRK just after phoning coastal batteries to stop hunting ships like the Blucher, which was sent to invade his country.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Knared ended a war that shares a name with this union.
swap.text: Name this union of Scandinavia first ruled by Eric of Pomerania to counter the influence of the Hanseatic League.
swap.clue: This polity was weakened by earlier rebellions led by Amund Bolt in one member and Engelbrekt in another, leading to the deposition of its monarch, Eric of Pomerania.

question.leadin: Answer the following about explorers who may or may not have discovered the New World.
question.text: This Icelandic explorer is the first known European to have set foot on continental North America. His visit to "Vinland" has been tentatively identified with the archaeological site of L'Anse aux ["LAN sow"] Meadows in Newfoundland.
question.clue: This explorer earned the nickname "Lucky" after rescuing a shipwrecked crew.

swap.leadin: A king of this name won the province of Hising after winning a dice game because one of his dice split into two, leaving a sum of 7.
swap.text: Name that king, who had the surname Haraldsson. Another king of this name with the surname Tryggvason ["trig-VAS-son"] converted Norway to Christianity and baptized Leif Ericson.
swap.clue: A statue in Trondheim commemorates that king of this name referred to as Tryggvason ].

question.leadin: This scientist claimed he "lived like a sage and died like a fool" after he refused to use the restroom at a banquet and died of a bladder or kidney condition.
question.text: Name this scientist who constructed the Uraniborg observatory as Lord of Hven. He wore a brass nose after losing a duel.
question.clue: This Danish scientist and author of Introduction to the New Astronomy died after contracting a kidney ailment that was brought on by a banquet in which he refused to leave the table to relieve himself so as to avoid committing a social faux pas.

swap.leadin: To flout a Prussian ban on this flag, farmers bred a so-called "protest pig" whose coloration was meant to resemble it.
swap.text: Name this national flag. After a prayer by Archbishop Anders Sunesen, this flag supposedly fell from the sky during the 1219 Battle of Lyndanisse ("lin-duh-NISS-uh").

question.text: This Norwegian claim, located between the British and Australian claims at 20 degrees West and around 44 degrees East, was named by Roald Amundsen after the wife of King Haakon VII.
question.clue: The Prime Meridian also passes through this Antarctic region. Claimed by Norway, this region is named for the wife of King Haakon VII ["the seventh"], who reigned from 1905 to 1957, and who was also the daughter of King Edward VII ["the seventh"] of Great Britain.

swap.leadin: After his sister married James I, a king of this name often visited for alcohol-soaked soirees, including one where he ruined a play by getting the actors drunk, and then collapsed after being "smeared with jelly and cream."
swap.text: Give this name of ten kings who ruled the same country as part of the House of Oldenburg. A king of this name briefly and inconsequentially intervened in the Thirty Years' War, before he withdrew under the Treaty of Lubeck.
swap.answerHtml: Christian [accept Christian IV; accept, but DO NOT REVEAL, any numbered Christian of Denmark] (The sister in the lead-in is Anne of Denmark.)
swap.clue: The second king of this name was anointed by Gustav Trolle, and notably ordered that the bodies of Sten Sture the Younger be exhumed and set on fire during a visit to Stockholm.

question.text: Due to skepticism over Henson's voyage, the first undisputed expedition to the North Pole was led by this Norwegian explorer, the first to reach the South Pole and traverse the Northwest Passage.
question.clue: This person led the crew that disappeared searching for the airship Italia and was the first to successfully navigate the North-west Passage in a boat, the Gjoa .

swap.text: The name of this Norwegian archipelago means "cold shores," and its three inhabited islands are Spitzbergen, Bear Island, and Hopen.
swap.clue: This Norwegian territory's namesake treaty regulates commercial and military activities. This Arctic archipelago is home to one of the largest seed banks in the world -- the Global Seed Vault.

question.text: Finnish became an official language of administration during an "Age of" this concept in Sweden. That era named for this concept saw increased parliamentary power after the Great Northern War.
question.answerHtml: Age of Liberty [accept frihetstiden or frihet; accept vapauden aika or vapautta]
question.clue: This era follows an era of imperialism called the Stormaktstiden ("STORM-okts-tee-den").

swap.text: Hone Heke cut down James Busby's flagstaff to start the First Maori War, which is often described with this term. It is also applied to a "Great" conflict fought between Charles XII and Peter the Great.
swap.clue: The second conflict of this name saw Azov returned to the Ottoman Turks following their victory at the Battle of Pruth River.

question.leadin: The Kuli stone, now found in a museum in this city, describes how a lord who ruled from here tried to force subjects to convert to Christianity.
question.text: Name this city founded in 997 by Olaf Tryggvason, the medieval capital of Norway.
question.clue: Jon remained loyal to this city's exiled archbishop Olav Engelbrektsson, who led the Norwegian Riksrad ("reeks-ROAD") until its 1537 dissolution with the Reformation. Pilgrims visited Saint Olaf's shrine at this city's cathedral.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about cities associated with the Hanseatic League.
swap.text: King Valdemar IV threatened to sack this city unless it filled three beer barrels with plunder. The Victual Brothers had their headquarters in this city that, along with The Hague, names a set of rules adopted in 1924 to govern maritime transport of goods.
swap.clue: Even before the Hanseatic League's inception, this city on the island of Gotland was a major Baltic trading hub. After capturing this city from the Hansa, the Victual Brothers used it as a base for conducting piracy.

question.text: Following the Battle of Poltava, Lewanhaupt and Charles adandoned everything leading to this time period of Norwegian history in which the Russians decimated the population of Norway.
question.answerHtml: The Greater Wrath [accept: isoviha from Will Alston; accept The Great Discord]

swap.text: The Norwegian language debate erupted after Norwegian elites began favoring an independent language during Norway's union with Sweden under this royal family, established by a Napoleonic general who took the regnal name Charles XIV.
swap.clue: The founder of this dynasty was once implicated in the Rennes Plot, and became the governor of Hanover and Bremen before being awarded the title of Prince of Pontecorvo.
